title: At-Tin 95:6-8 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-'Alaq 13 to 19, At-Tin and meem sakinah
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 26 (Pupil PDF worksheet: At-Tin 95:6-8 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 26. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍۢ (٦) فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِٱلدِّينِ (٧) أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted.
So what yet causes you to deny the Recompense?
Is not Allah the most just of judges?

keywords.def: the Recompense, the Day of Judgement

questions.q: Chunk and link At-Tin 95:6-8 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 95:6-8 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: The answer to 95:8 'Is not Allah the most just of judges?' is ...
Listening rota: today's group recites 95:6-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Recite all of At-Tin 95:1 to 8 to a partner. Partner marks any missed rule.
questions.a: Eight ayat with the rules applied.

questions.q: Label every meem sakinah and noon sakinah rule in 95:6.
questions.a: فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ izhar shafawi; أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ izhar (tanween before غ); مَمْنُونٍۢ izhar shafawi.

options: Those who believe and do righteous deeds
questions.a: A) Those who believe and do righteous deeds. 95:6: 'Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted.'

questions.q: How many ayat are in At-Tin?
Think again: At-Tin ends with a question: 'Is not Allah the most just of judges?' How would you answer, and why?
questions.a: Yes! Allah is the most just: He rewards belief and good deeds and never wrongs anyone.
